name: Apple Tree
intro: An apple tree is a fruit tree. It grows apples that we can eat.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: An apple tree has a wide, round top.
Its leaves are oval with a pointy tip.
In spring, it has white or pink flowers.
Each flower has 5 petals.
In fall, apples hang from its branches.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Apple trees first grew in Central Asia.
Now people grow them all over the world.
Most grow in the top half of the world.
People grow apple trees on farms and in yards.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: An apple tree needs lots of sun.
It likes sun for 8 hours each day.
Its soil must not stay soggy.
It needs a good drink of water each week.
It needs pollen from a different kind of apple tree.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: In winter, the apple tree rests.
In spring, new leaves and flowers grow.
Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Then the petals fall, and a tiny apple grows.
In fall, the apples are ripe and ready to pick.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: There are thousands of kinds of apples.
Apple trees are in the rose family.
Inside an apple, the seeds sit in a star shape.
Apples get sweeter just before they are picked.
An apple tree can live 100 years or more.

vocab.meaning: A yellow dust that flowers need to make fruit and seeds.
Ready to pick and eat.
A tiny part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
The dirt that plants grow in.

name: Bald Eagle
intro: A bald eagle is a big bird with a white head. It lives near water in North America.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A bald eagle is a very big bird.
It has a white head and a white tail.
Its body and wings are dark brown.
It has a yellow beak and yellow feet.
Its open wings are wider than a grown-up is tall.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Bald eagles live in North America.
They live near water.
They like lakes, rivers, and the coast.
Many bald eagles live in Alaska and Canada.
They build nests at the top of tall trees.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Bald eagles are predators.
They eat mostly fish.
They swoop low over the water.
They catch fish with their feet.
They also eat ducks and small animals.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A mother eagle usually lays two eggs.
Both parents take turns keeping the eggs warm.
Baby eagles are called eaglets.
Eaglets are gray at first and then turn brown.
They get white heads at about four or five years old.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A bald eagle is not really bald.
Its head is covered with white feathers.
Bald eagles can spot a fish from far away.
The bald eagle is a symbol of the United States.
The biggest eagle nest ever found was as heavy as a car.

vocab.meaning: A baby eagle.
An animal that hunts other animals for food.
The land right next to the ocean.
A picture or thing that stands for something else.

name: Bamboo
intro: Bamboo is a giant grass. It is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Bamboo is a giant grass, not a tree.
Its stems are tall and hollow inside.
The stems have rings called joints.
Branches and leaves grow from the joints.
Some bamboo is small, and some is taller than a house.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Wild bamboo grows in Asia, Africa, and the Americas.
Many kinds grow where it is warm all year.
Other kinds can live where winters are cold.
Bamboo often grows close together in big clumps.
One bamboo plant can spread into a whole forest.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: Bamboo needs plenty of light.
It needs soil that drains well.
It needs water, but not too much.
Warm-weather bamboo can die if it freezes.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: New bamboo stems are called shoots.
Shoots come up from stems under the ground.
A shoot grows straight up very fast.
Some bamboo can grow as tall as a first grader in one day!
Most bamboo makes flowers only once in many years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Giant pandas eat almost nothing but bamboo.
Red pandas and some lemurs eat bamboo too.
People build houses and bridges with bamboo.
Bamboo can be made into paper, chopsticks, and cloth.
Bamboo grows back quickly after it is cut.

vocab.meaning: A plant with long, thin leaves, like the grass in a lawn.
Empty inside, like a straw.
A new stem that is just starting to grow.
A ring on a bamboo stem where branches can grow.

name: Bat
intro: A bat is a mammal that can fly. It sleeps upside down during the day.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A bat has a furry body.
Its wings are thin skin with no fur.
The skin stretches between long finger bones.
Many bats have big ears.
The biggest bats have wings wider than a grown-up is tall.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Bats live almost everywhere on Earth.
They do not live in the coldest places.
Bats rest in caves, trees, and buildings.
Some bats sleep through the winter.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Most bats eat insects.
Some bats eat fruit.
Some bats drink nectar from flowers.
Fruit bats find food by sight and smell.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby bat is called a pup.
A mother bat usually has one pup a year.
A new pup has no fur and its eyes are closed.
The pup drinks its mother's milk.
It learns to fly in a few weeks.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
Bats hang upside down to rest.
Some bats find food by listening to echoes.
Bats help plants by carrying pollen and seeds.
Bats are not blind; they can see.

vocab.meaning: An animal with fur or hair that drinks milk from its mom as a baby.
Finding things by making sounds and listening for echoes.
A sweet juice inside flowers.
Yellow dust that flowers need to make seeds.

photos.alt: A bat with big ears flying with its wings open
A flying fox bat hanging upside down with its wings spread

name: Dandelion
intro: A dandelion is a bright yellow flower. Its seeds float away on the wind.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A dandelion has a bright yellow flower.
The flower is made of many tiny flowers.
Its leaves have jagged edges like teeth.
Its stem is hollow inside.
A broken stem has white, milky juice.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Dandelions first grew in Europe and Asia.
Now they grow on every continent but Antarctica.
They grow in lawns, fields, and gardens.
They can even grow in sidewalk cracks.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A dandelion grows well in full sun.
It likes deep soil that drains well.
It can grow in many kinds of soil.
Its seeds need light to sprout.
It needs some water to keep the soil damp.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A dandelion grows a long root called a taproot.
The root stores food through the winter.
The plant comes back every spring.
The yellow flower turns into a white puffball.
Each seed has a tiny parachute that floats on the wind.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: The name dandelion means "lion's tooth" in French.
The flower opens in the day and closes at night.
Bees visit dandelions for food in early spring.
One flower can make hundreds of seeds.
Its root can grow deeper than a grown-up is tall.

vocab.meaning: One long, thick root that grows straight down.
The white puffball full of seeds.
Empty inside, like a straw.
One of the seven very large pieces of land on Earth.

name: Flamingo
intro: A flamingo is a tall pink bird. It wades in shallow water.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A flamingo is a tall pink bird.
It has very long, thin legs.
Its long neck can bend like the letter S.
Its beak bends down in the middle.
The biggest kind can be taller than a first grader.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Flamingos live in shallow water.
They live in lagoons and lakes.
Some of these lakes have salty water.
American flamingos live on islands in the Caribbean Sea.
Flamingos live together in big groups called colonies.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Flamingos eat shrimp, snails, and algae.
A flamingo puts its head upside down in the water.
Its beak works like a strainer to catch food.
Their pink color comes from the food they eat.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Flamingo parents build a little hill of mud for a nest.
The mother lays one egg on top.
The egg hatches after about one month.
The chick is fluffy and gray or white.
It turns pink as it grows up.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A new chick is about the size of a tennis ball.
Parents feed their chick a kind of milk from their bodies.
Flamingos run on the water before they fly.
Flamingos hear well, but they can barely smell.
A flamingo can live for a very long time.

vocab.meaning: Tiny plant-like living things that grow in water.
A big group of animals that live together.
A baby bird.
A shallow pool of salty water near the ocean.

name: Giant Panda
intro: A giant panda is a black and white bear. It lives in the mountains of China.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A giant panda is a big bear.
Its fur is black and white.
It has black ears and black patches around its eyes.
Its legs and shoulders are black too.
Its fur is thick and woolly.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Giant pandas live in China.
They live in forests high in the mountains.
Lots of bamboo grows in these forests.
Pandas are shy and stay away from people.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: A panda eats mostly bamboo.
It eats for about 12 hours every day.
It holds bamboo with a wrist bone that works like a thumb.
Its strong jaws and flat teeth crush the stems.
Sometimes it eats grass, fruit, or bugs.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby panda is called a cub.
A new cub is pink and has no fur.
It is about as small as a stick of butter.
Its eyes open when it is about 2 months old.
The cub stays with its mom for more than a year.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Pandas like to do somersaults.
Pandas are strong swimmers.
Pandas can bleat, honk, and growl.
Some pandas do handstands against trees.
People call the panda the bamboo bear.

vocab.meaning: A tall, tough grass with hard stems.
A baby bear.
An animal with fur or hair that drinks milk from its mom as a baby.

name: Gorilla
intro: A gorilla is the biggest ape in the world. It lives in forests in Africa.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Gorillas have black or dark brown hair.
They have no hair on their faces.
Their arms are longer than their legs.
Grown-up males have silver hair on their backs.
A big male can be as heavy as three grown-ups.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Gorillas live in Africa.
They live in rainforests and mountain forests.
They spend most of their time on the ground.
Each night, a gorilla makes a nest of leaves to sleep in.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Gorillas eat mostly plants.
They eat leaves, stems, and fruit.
Sometimes they eat ants or other bugs.
A big male eats a lot of food every day.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Gorillas live in family groups called troops.
A big male called a silverback leads the troop.
A baby gorilla rides on its mother's back.
Young gorillas sleep in their mother's nest.
Young gorillas play games like follow the leader.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Every gorilla has its own nose print.
Gorillas are gentle and calm.
Baby gorillas have a white tuft of hair on their bottoms.
A gorilla's big toe can grab like a thumb.
Gorillas have been seen using tools.

vocab.meaning: A big animal like a monkey that has no tail.
A family group of gorillas.
A grown-up male gorilla with silver hair on his back.
A warm forest where it rains a lot.

name: Honeybee
intro: A honeybee is a small insect that makes honey. It lives with many other bees in a hive.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A honeybee is a small insect.
A worker bee is about as long as a grown-up's fingernail.
Its body is covered with tiny hairs.
Worker bees have pollen baskets on their back legs.
The queen bee is bigger than the workers.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Honeybees live in a home called a hive.
Many bees live together in a colony.
One hive can hold thousands of bees.
Bees build honeycomb out of wax.
Each little room in the comb has six sides.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Honeybees visit flowers for food.
They drink sweet nectar from flowers.
They also collect pollen.
Bees turn nectar into honey.
In winter, bees eat the honey they saved.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Each hive has one queen bee.
The queen lays the eggs.
A baby bee is called a larva.
The larva eats pollen and honey.
Then it changes into a grown-up bee.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Bees dance to show other bees where food is.
Bees help plants make fruits and vegetables.
Honeybees sting only to protect their hive.
Honey color depends on the flowers bees visit.
One worker makes only a tiny bit of honey in her life.

vocab.meaning: The home where a group of bees lives.
A big group of animals that live together.
A sweet juice inside flowers.
A yellow powder that flowers make.
A baby insect that looks like a little worm.

name: Kangaroo
intro: A kangaroo is an animal that hops on its back legs. It lives in Australia.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A kangaroo has big, strong back legs.
It has small front legs.
It has a long, strong tail.
A big kangaroo can be taller than a grown-up.
A mother kangaroo has a pouch on her belly.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Big kangaroos live only in Australia.
They live in groups.
A group of kangaroos is called a mob.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Kangaroos eat plants.
They mostly eat grass.
They also eat small bushes called shrubs.
Red kangaroos can go a long time without water.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
A new joey is about as small as a grape.
It crawls into its mom's pouch all by itself.
It drinks milk and grows in the pouch.
It stays in the pouch for many months.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A kangaroo can jump as far as two cars parked in a row.
It can hop as fast as a car on a town street.
Its tail helps it balance when it jumps.
Kangaroos are good swimmers.
Kangaroos thump their feet to warn others of danger.

vocab.meaning: An animal mom that carries her baby in a pouch.
A baby kangaroo.
A pocket of skin on a mother's belly.
A group of kangaroos.

name: Koala
intro: A koala is a furry animal that lives in trees. It lives in Australia.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A koala looks like a teddy bear.
But a koala is not a bear.
It has round, fuzzy ears.
Its fur feels rough, not soft.
It has sharp claws for climbing trees.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Koalas live in Australia.
They live in eucalyptus forests.
They stay high up in the trees.
They come down only to move to a new tree.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves.
They are very picky eaters.
They eat only a few kinds of eucalyptus.
Koalas eat a little dirt to help their tummies.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby koala is called a joey.
A new joey is as small as a jelly bean.
It lives in its mom's pouch for about 6 months.
Then it rides on its mom's back.
At about 1 year old, it eats only leaves.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.

name: Ladybug
intro: A ladybug is a small, round beetle. Many ladybugs are red with black spots.

A sugar maple leaf has five main parts called lobes.

sentences: Maple trees grow in North America, Europe, and Asia.
Most kinds of maples come from Asia.
Sugar maples grow in the northern United States and Canada.
People plant maples in parks and yards for shade.

sections.title: What does it need?

Young sugar maples can grow in shade.

Salt from roads can hurt sugar maples.

The young tree grows a little taller each year.
A sugar maple makes its first seeds at about 30 years old.
Some sugar maples live for hundreds of years.

A maple leaf is on the flag of Canada.

Bees visit maple flowers in early spring.

name: Monarch Butterfly
intro: A monarch is a big orange and black butterfly. Many monarchs fly far away each fall.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A monarch is a big orange butterfly.
Its wings have black lines and black edges.
Small white dots sit on the black edges.
Its open wings are about as wide as a grown-up's hand.
A monarch weighs about as much as a paper clip.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Many monarchs live in North America.
They need fields, yards, and gardens with flowers.
In the fall, many monarchs migrate south.
Some fly all the way to Mexico.
Others spend the winter in California.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: A monarch caterpillar eats only milkweed.
Grown-up monarchs drink nectar from flowers.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A monarch starts as a tiny egg on milkweed.
A striped caterpillar hatches out.
It eats and grows for about two weeks.
Then it makes a green chrysalis with gold dots.
A butterfly comes out one or two weeks later.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Bright orange wings tell birds not to eat them.
Millions of monarchs fly south together.
No one monarch makes the whole trip there and back.
Summer monarchs live only a few weeks.
Monarchs that fly south can live many months.

Grown-up sunflowers mostly face east.
One flower head can hold hundreds of seeds.
Bees visit sunflowers for nectar and pollen.
Kansas is called the Sunflower State.

name: Venus Flytrap
intro: A Venus flytrap is a small plant that catches bugs. Its leaves snap shut like a trap.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A Venus flytrap is a small green plant.
Its leaves grow in a circle.
Each leaf ends in a trap with two halves.
Tiny trigger hairs grow inside the trap.
Spiky bristles line the edges of the trap.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Venus flytraps grow wild in North Carolina and South Carolina.
They live in wet, sunny places like bogs.
The soil there is wet most of the year.
That soil has very little plant food.
Fires help keep their homes open and sunny.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A Venus flytrap needs lots of sun.
It needs wet soil.
It makes food from sunlight like other plants.
It also catches bugs to get extra nutrients.
It mostly eats ants and spiders.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A Venus flytrap grows from a tiny black seed.
In late spring, it grows white flowers.
The flowers sit on a tall stalk, away from the traps.
Each trap can close only a few times.
Then the plant grows a new trap.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A trap snaps shut very, very fast.
A hair must be touched two times to close the trap.
This way, raindrops do not trick the trap.
A trap cannot hurt people.
A Venus flytrap can live up to 20 years.

vocab.meaning: A plant that catches and eats bugs.
Wet, soft land with lots of water in the ground.
Things in food and soil that help living things grow.
Tiny hairs inside the trap that tell it to close.

name: Wolf
intro: A wolf is a wild animal in the dog family. Wolves live and hunt together in family groups.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A wolf looks like a big dog.
It has long legs and a bushy tail.
Its fur can be gray, brown, black, or white.
It is the biggest wild animal in the dog family.
Males are bigger than females.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Wolves live in North America, Europe, and Asia.
Many wolves live in Alaska and Canada.
They can live where it is very cold or very hot.
Each pack has its own home area called a territory.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Wolves eat meat.
They hunt big animals like deer, elk, and moose.
The pack hunts together as a team.
A wolf can eat as much meat as a big turkey in one meal.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby wolf is called a pup.
Pups are born in a den.
At first, pups cannot see or hear.
Older brothers and sisters help feed and play with the pups.
Young wolves stay with their parents for at least two years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Every wolf pack has its own howl.
A howl can be heard miles away.
Wolves bow to ask another wolf to play.
A wolf's nose smells much better than yours.
Wolves and dogs are close relatives.

vocab.meaning: A family group of wolves.
A baby wolf.
A long, loud call that wolves make.
The home area where an animal lives and finds food.
